violations.title: RTE TCS Commercially Processed Food, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is commercially processed is not used or discarded within 24 hours of when the original container was opened and is not observed to be date marked: Pre-made slices of cake were taken out of the original container and separated into smaller containers that were not date marked. The slices of cake are stored in the 2DR UPR cooler in the lobby.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety commercially processed foods when opened and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of the original container was opened. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. This date cannot exceed any manufacturer determined 'use-by' date based on food safety. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL COMMERCIALLY PROCESSED FOODS, WHEN TAKEN OUT OF THEIR ORIGINAL CONTAINER MUST HAVE A DATE MARK LABLED ON THEM. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE BEING WRITING THE PROPER DATE MARK ON THE SLICES OF CAKE AT TIME OF INSPECTION.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: cut tomatoes(50F) ; shredded lettuce (51F); cooked noodles (50F) in the walk-in refrigerator were temping above the required 41F or below.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL COLD FOODS NEED TO BE COLD HELD AT A MAXIMUM TEMPERATURE OF 41F OR BELOW TO PREVENT THE POTENTIAL SPREAD OF BACTERIA. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE THROW AWAY SLICED TOMATOES, CUT LETTUCE, AND COOKED NOODLES.
